subject: Operational tolerance window for cross-region failover (RTO/RPO discussion)

From: Maria Lopez <maria@finbank.com>

Cc: procurement@finbank.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operational tolerance for cross-region failover

Stephanie,

Thanks for the product walkthrough yesterday — the demo was helpful. We’re trying to reconcile our internal DR obligations with the operational realities of a multi-region deployment. FinBank’s ops policy currently expects RTO <= 1 minute and RPO <= 1 second for any customer-facing inference request. That’s been flagged by our SREs as potentially infeasible without an active-active topology for all endpoints.

Can Redwood confirm whether you can meet hard 1-minute RTO / sub-second RPO for the Redwood hosted API across active failover between us-west and us-east? If not, can you propose an explicit operational tolerance window or a limited exception we can take to our compliance board (e.g., 10 minute RTO with bounded data loss, or an agreed warm-standby activation window)?

For context I attached a small extract of our observed latencies and request patterns. Procurement suggests we document any carveouts clearly in the SOW. Looking for a technical note and a recommended contractual scope we can use.

Best,
Maria Lopez
Sr. Cloud Reliability Manager
FinBank

Subject: Re: Operational tolerance for cross-region failover

Hi Maria — thanks for the note and the metrics; this is exactly the right place to start. Short answer: we can offer a couple of defensible, auditable options but the hard 1-minute RTO / sub-second RPO for arbitrary endpoints without provisioning active-active across regions is not something we guarantee on the hosted tiers today.

Options we recommend (summary):
- Option A — Active-Active (fully geo-replicated): RTO < 1 minute, RPO ~0 (writes synchronously mirrored). Requires dedicated capacity in both regions and a DNS/edge front-door with <10s cutover TTL. Higher monthly commitment.
- Option B — Warm-standby with fast failover: RTO 5–15 minutes, RPO under 30s using continuous KV sync + replay. Lower cost than A; we can scope a 'fast-activation' runbook and test cadence.
- Option C — Standby with queued replay: RTO 10–60 minutes, RPO dependent on last checkpoint (we can cap at 5 minutes if you accept short buffering). Least expensive but has potential brief degraded availability window.

I've asked Laura (runtime) to provide measured failover delta times from our recent inter-region tests so you have data to present to your compliance board. Karthik will advise on language you can use in the SOW to limit liability while providing a clear operational tolerance window.

I’ll attach a proposal matrix outlining costs, SLOs, and the recommended acceptance tests. Happy to schedule a call with your SREs.

—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Product — Redwood Inference

Maria — adding a short technical breakdown from the runtime/infra side. We ran a controlled failover test (us-west -> us-east) across a production-like traffic profile last quarter; the measured deltas were:

- Control-plane detection + policy routing switch: median 6s, 95th percentile 22s (depends on BGP/edge caches).
- KV cache warm-up (per-session): median 8s additional for common prefixes; 95th percentile 90s for cold workloads.
- Model cold-start (if model queueing/scale-up required): variable — from 30s to 6m depending on quantization/instance type.

Bottom line: if you run active-active with mirrored state, you can achieve the 1 minute objective for the majority of traffic. If you rely on warm-standby, realistic RTOs fall into the 5–15 minute band unless you accept larger reserved capacity and some pre-warmed instances.

Suggested acceptance test (we can run and provide logs):
1) 30-minute soak with synthetic traffic; 2) Trigger route drain in primary region; 3) Measure 95th percentile tail latency and successful-inference rate during window.

If you want, we can provide the raw csv from our test run (summaries included in our Drive link).

—Laura Bennett
Sr. Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

Folks — quick note from contracts/legal. If FinBank needs a bounded tolerance window rather than the hard RTO/RPO, we can agree to a scoped SLA carveout. Key items we need to capture in the SOW:

- Exact scope (API routes, model versions, customer-owned keys) — carveout applies only to listed endpoints; everything else remains under standard SLOs.
- Activation criteria for failover and who authorizes (FinBank ops vs. Redwood support).
- Acceptance testing cadence and observability hooks (we’ll provide trace-level telemetry for each test).
- Financial remedies: a defined credit schedule for breaches within the agreed tolerance window.
- Cap on aggregate liability for failover-related incidents.

I’ll draft suggested contract language and propose a short addendum. Also recommend a 6-month review after go-live to revise the tolerance window based on observed metrics.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

Thanks all — this is helpful and aligns with what I expected from the SRE review. Procurement is OK with a scoped tolerance window if we get:

1) A written SOW addendum that lists the endpoints covered and an explicit RTO/RPO matrix (we’re prioritizing payment endpoints first).
2) An acceptance test within 30 days of go-live with raw logs delivered to our SREs.
3) A 6-month operational review and ability to tighten the window if metrics allow.

We’ll proceed with Option B (warm-standby fast activation) for the initial deployment to control cost, but we want Redwood to document the activation runbook and the rollback criteria. Can your team send the SOW addendum draft and a proposed test window next week?

Maria Lopez
